failure_reasons.judge_reason: The paper's breadth summary reports that 'A single specification-conditioned model jointly supports two IC families, three boundary-condition types (periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann), and three PDE families (reaction–diffusion, reaction, and diffusion)'. The run logs contradict this breadth count. Every meta.json trains on exactly one family: reaction runs on reaction; RD runs on reaction_diffusion with periodic BC only; BC runs on diffusion with periodic+Dirichlet. run_experiments.py accepts a single --family, and run_bc_experiments.py is diffusion-only. So the number of PDE families jointly supported by any single logged model is one, and the RD/reaction models support only periodic BC. This is a breadth value contradicted by its source, not merely untraced. Latent statistics are mostly traceable: min pairwise latent distance 0.7073 and Pearson r=0.6604 match diagnostics.json, and the PCA projections are ordered by A and sigma. The claim that the first two PCs carry '>99%' of the variance, however, contradicts the logged 0.9719+0.0141=0.986. That is minor on its own and is not the basis of the verdict.

The paper describes the 'learned function encoder' as the samples passed through 'the dedicated function encoder described above' (the residual LayerNorm/skip encoder). The 'learned' arm reported in Table 1 is build_model('learned') -> StructuredModel, a plain tanh 32->64->64->32. Its completed 3-seed results show large shared-condition regression (structured 0.1237 and naive 0.1812 vs baseline 0.0724, far outside the pre-registered max(10%, 0.005) rule) and the structured arm worse than naive on the unseen family (0.676 vs 0.480).
